```{r loadlib, results='hide', message=F, warning=F}
library(zoo)
library(magrittr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(rcompanion)
library(here)
library(glmnet)
library(lubridate)
```

```{r reading data}
demographic <- read.csv(here("GRLS_data/dog_profile.csv"))
labs <- read.csv(here("GRLS_data/clinical_labs.csv"))
physical <- read.csv(here("GRLS_data/exam_physical.csv"))

# We want to use CBC blood metrics
labs_cbc <- subset(labs, test_group == "Complete Blood Count" & vet_visit_type == "annual") %>% unique()

# Since we need to control for body size, we need to only use dogs with a weight listed
physical_weight <- subset(physical, complete.cases(weight))

# We're only interested in dogs for which demographic data, weight, and cbc are all available.
demographic %<>% subset(subject_id %in% physical_weight$subject_id & subject_id %in% labs_cbc$subject_id)

nrow(demographic)
```

```{r  cleaning demographic data}
# Event type for censoring. TRUE = death, False = all other outcomes
demographic$event_type <- demographic$death_date != ""

# Reduce all event dates to a single column
demographic <- unite(demographic, withdrawn_date, inactive_date, death_date, sep = "") %>% rename(event_date = withdrawn_date)

# If no other event date, include date when data released.
# This would represent the last follow-up, since the demographic data is released with no embargo.
demographic$event_date %<>% sub(pattern = "^$", replacement = "2025-01")

# Convert to year-month date type to allow for numeric operations
demographic$birth_date %<>% as.yearmon()
demographic$event_date %<>% as.yearmon()
demographic[demographic$subject_id=="grlsR2FVJBB","event_date"] <- as.yearmon("2023-01") # fixing incorrect death date; see grls_init_expl

# Determine age at event (in years)
demographic$event_age <-demographic$event_date - demographic$birth_date

# Clean up, keep only relevant variables
demographic %<>% select(subject_id, sex_status, birth_date, event_date, event_age, event_type) %>%
  na.omit()
```

```{r cleaning weight and labs metadata}
# Remove all non-weight variables (and remove any incomplete entries)
physical_weight %<>% select(subject_id, record_date, weight) %>%
  rename(weight_date = record_date) %>%
  subset(weight_date != "") %>%
  na.omit()

# Convert to year-month date type
physical_weight$weight_date %<>% as.yearmon()

# Merge with demographic to determine age (in years) at record date
physical_weight %<>% merge(select(demographic, subject_id, birth_date, sex_status), by = "subject_id")
physical_weight$weight_age <- physical_weight$weight_date - physical_weight$birth_date
physical_weight$sex_status %<>% as.factor()

# Convert lab dates to year-month date type
labs_cbc$visit_date <- parse_date_time(labs_cbc$visit_date, orders = c("ym", "mdy"))
labs_cbc$visit_date %<>% as.yearmon()

# Include only subjects who are not censored (i.e. death date is known)
labs_cbc <- labs_cbc[labs_cbc$subject_id %in% demographic[which(demographic$event_type), "subject_id"],]

# Merge with demographic to determine age (in years) at record date
labs_cbc %<>% merge(select(demographic, subject_id, birth_date, event_age, sex_status), by = "subject_id")
labs_cbc$visit_age <- labs_cbc$visit_date - labs_cbc$birth_date
labs_cbc$sex_status %<>% as.factor()

# Divide age at record date by age at death to determine percentage of life lived at record
labs_cbc$visit_pll <- labs_cbc$visit_age / labs_cbc$event_age
```

```{r Weight Join}
labs_cbc <- inner_join( # Keep only rows with values in both tables
  labs_cbc, select(physical_weight, -birth_date, -sex_status),
  join_by(subject_id, closest(visit_age >= weight_age)) # Rolling join, carry over last weight measurement
  ) %>% 
  subset(visit_age - weight_age <= 1) # Pipe to subset and remove all weight measures >1 yr old

# Histogram to visualize the distribution of time between RDW and weight measures
hist(labs_cbc$visit_age - labs_cbc$weight_age)
```

```{r Cleaning CBC data}
labs_cbc$test_name_units <- paste(labs_cbc$test_name, labs_cbc$test_units)
unique(labs_cbc$test_name_units)

table(labs_cbc$test_name, labs_cbc$test_units) # Check how many of ea. test, verify tests always in one unit

metrics_to_use <- c(
  "% Eosinophils %",
  "% Lymphocytes %",
  "% Monocytes %",
  "% Neutrophils %",
  "Hematocrit (HCT) %",
  "Hemoglobin (HGB) g/dL",
  "MPV fL",
  "RBC M/uL",
  "RDW %",
  "WBC K/uL"
) # Other metrics are either based on an already included metric, have no units, or are included in too few records

labs_cbc %<>% filter(test_name_units %in% metrics_to_use)

labs_cbc %<>% select(-test_name, -test_units, -ref_range_or_cutoff)

labs_cbc_pivot <- pivot_wider(labs_cbc, names_from = test_name_units, values_from = test_value) %>% unnest(cols = metrics_to_use) %>% na.omit()

labs_cbc_pivot[,metrics_to_use] <- sapply(labs_cbc_pivot[,metrics_to_use], as.numeric) # Convert all metrics to numeric
labs_cbc_pivot[,metrics_to_use] <- sapply(labs_cbc_pivot[,metrics_to_use], blom) # Normal scores transform data before fitting
labs_cbc_pivot$weight %<>% blom()
```


```{r}
set.seed(31415)
validation_subjects <- sample(unique(labs_cbc_pivot$subject_id), 0.3 * length(unique(labs_cbc_pivot$subject_id)))
validation_samples <- labs_cbc_pivot[labs_cbc_pivot$subject_id %in% validation_subjects,]
validation_x_df <- validation_samples %>% select(sex_status, weight, metrics_to_use)

fitting_subjects <- unique(labs_cbc_pivot[! labs_cbc_pivot$subject_id %in% validation_samples,]$subject_id)
fitting_samples <- labs_cbc_pivot[labs_cbc_pivot$subject_id %in% fitting_subjects,]
fitting_x_df <- fitting_samples %>% select(sex_status, weight, metrics_to_use)
```

```{r}
x_matrix <- makeX(
  train = fitting_x_df,
  test = validation_x_df,
  na.impute = TRUE
)

cv <- cv.glmnet(
  x = x_matrix$x,
  y = fitting_samples$visit_pll,
  alpha = 1,
  nfolds = 10
)

plot(cv)

glm <- glmnet(
  x = x_matrix$x,
  y = fitting_samples$visit_pll,
  alpha = 1,
  lambda = cv$lambda.min
)

assess_glm <- assess.glmnet(
  glm,
  newx = x_matrix$xtest,
  newy = validation_samples$visit_pll
)

```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
predict_test <- predict(glm, s = cv$lambda.min, newx = x_matrix$xtest)
colnames(predict_test) <- "predicted_PLL"
cor.test(validation_samples$visit_pll, predict_test)

plot_predict <- cbind(validation_samples, predict_test)
ggplot(plot_predict, aes(x = visit_pll, y = predicted_PLL)) + geom_point()
```
